title: Weibull Regression and Machine Learning Survival Models: Methodology, Comparison, and Application to Biomedical Data Related to Cardiac Surgery
summary: This paper presents a comparative study between Weibull regression and random survival forest (RSF) models for analyzing survival data from cardiac surgery patients. The models are evaluated using error rate, Harrell C-index, and variable importance, with RSF showing superior predictive performance (20.31% error rate) compared to Weibull (23.82%). The methodology is demonstrated on length of stay data from cardiac surgery patients at the Heart Institute of the University of São Paulo, Brazil.
